quote: Byte-identical notes across grouped legs render ONCE, at group level, on expand; a leg whose note text differs keeps its own.
why: This contradicts my AC-5 ("Expanding a group reveals the per-leg rows exactly as they render today: same fields, same not-a-number literals, same fidelity notes, same per-leg figures — nothing dropped, nothing added") and it contradicts the BRIEF's own wording, "expandable to today's per-leg rows unchanged". It also weakens the mitigation the whole withheld-aggregate story rests on: the reason a group may refuse to net is that per-leg truth stays fully visible underneath, and hoisting notes off the leg rows makes "today's rows, unchanged" no longer a checkable property. The wall UX designs against does not exist on the book this feature ships against: the owner's real book is 4 apparent two-leg groups plus 1 lone NVDA call, so the largest expanded group is 2 legs and 2 notes, not "five grouped legs × two notes = ten near-identical lines". I would rather pay 2 duplicate lines today than trade away the zero-regression property on the disclosure.
proposal: AC-5 stands for v1: leg rows inside the disclosure render exactly as they do today, notes included. Future-date the dedup, pinned to an observation rather than a hunch — if a real book ever produces a group whose expansion carries more than three identical note lines, dedup lands as its own change with a group-level note line that is ADDITIVE (nothing removed from the leg rows) or as a true hoist, decided then. If UX still wants the hoist in v1 after the 2-leg fact, it stops being a council question and becomes an owner question at R3, because it trades a BRIEF commitment for density.

quote: The count is shown on *every* option holding, grouped or not; the **expander exists only at two legs or more**.
why: My §2 rules a ticker with exactly one option leg renders today's row ungrouped and unchanged, and my §6.1 treats `1 option leg` as copy the formatter must handle but the surface never reaches. Three things push against showing it: (a) it adds a new visible string to the one broker row the owner live-verified byte-for-byte on 2026-08-05, and the architect's assumption 2 rests on that row keeping its zero-regression property; (b) the leg count's job, in PM's own words, is that it 'is what makes the collapse safe to trust' — on a row where nothing is collapsed it has no job; (c) a solitary '1 option leg' invites precisely the reading PM forbids two sentences earlier, 'Not "this is a single-leg trade"', because a count of one on a row with no expander reads as a completeness claim about the trade rather than a fact about the feed.
proposal: The leg count renders only where a collapse hides rows — i.e. on group headers at ≥2 legs. The lone NVDA call keeps today's row unchanged, and the missing expander is not the only difference between it and a group, it simply is not a group. If PM still wants uniformity, then the lone row's count must be the same mono/secondary treatment with the `grouped by underlying` clause omitted (nothing was grouped), and AC-23 stays `review` and non-blocking — but I would rather not put the string there.

quote: With every group collapsed, the sum of the groups' leg counts plus the ungrouped rows equals the position count the broker reported. Collapsing never makes a position unreachable or uncounted.
why: This equates a LEG count with a POSITION count. It is true today only by coincidence — the architect carries `position_count` and `leg_count` as two fields precisely because 'Under the Webull adapter every option row maps to exactly one leg... A future adapter (SnapTrade) can return a true multi-leg position and they diverge.' A test written to AC-6 as phrased pins the coincidence rather than the invariant, and it would go green on the day the two numbers stop meaning the same thing. This is the data half of my own R1 Risk 5: the header says '4 option legs' and the expansion shows rows, so the moment one position carries two legs the visible count becomes a quiet lie about what is behind the chevron.
proposal: Split the claim. Nothing-is-lost is a POSITION invariant: the sum of the groups' member-position counts plus the ungrouped rows equals the broker's position count (`test`, blocks the ship). The header's visible number stays `leg_count` with the noun 'legs' (`review`), and a second criterion pins that the noun tracks the number — if the header says legs, expanding must reveal that many legs, not that many rows. Today the two criteria are satisfied by the same book; tomorrow they are not, and the copy is the thing that breaks.
